title: 2 MUST OWN ETFs as Tech Stocks CRASH
creator: Mark Roussin CPA
summary: Mark Roussin frames a tech sell-off driven by AI-spending, inflation and Federal Reserve worries — the Nasdaq-100 down more than 6% in two weeks and the S&P 500 down about 2% on his stated figures — and previews a heavy week: the Fed meeting on 27–28 October, PCE inflation data and roughly 180 earnings reports. His answer is to complement a tech-heavy portfolio with two dividend ETFs he calls must-own. SCHD, the Schwab US Dividend Equity ETF, is a top-five holding, up 27% year to date against the S&P's 11% on his figures, yielding about 3% with 14 consecutive years of dividend growth, a 0.06% expense ratio and roughly 100 holdings screened on cash flow, profitability and dividend growth rather than yield alone. HDV, the iShares Core High Dividend ETF, is the higher-yield, more defensive second name: up 24% year to date, a yield above 3%, 0.08% fees and about 80 holdings tilted to staples, energy, healthcare and utilities — the four sectors that led the past month — with technology only about 1%. He cautions that the two overlap (both hold Chevron, Procter & Gamble and Verizon) and that HDV's top ten are 55% of the fund. The calls are SCHD — BUY reiterated and HDV — BUY, first tracked.

calls.thesis: BUY reiterated (was BUY 2026-10-06; no flip) — Schwab US Dividend Equity ETF is a top-five holding and 'a must-own in my eyes' and 'the dividend ETF': the greatest complement to a tech-heavy portfolio. Up 27% YTD stated (vs SPY +11%), without dividends. No share price stated.
calls.base_case: Focuses on established US dividend payers screened on cash flow, profitability, yield and dividend growth, not yield alone; 3% yield, dividend growth for 14 consecutive years, 0.06% expense ratio, ~100 holdings led by healthcare, staples, tech and energy (TXN, QCOM, PG, KO, CVX among largest).
calls.bull_case: Defensive sectors leading the past month (staples +10%, energy +9%, healthcare +7%, utilities +5% stated) are SCHD's strength, so it balances tech selling while earnings growth (~30% YoY pace stated for S&P 500) resets valuations.
calls.bear_case: Growth is slower and tech exposure is limited — the criticism he acknowledges; owning SCHD and HDV together overlaps (both hold CVX, PG, VZ), so it does not double diversification.

calls.thesis: BUY (first tracked HDV call for Mark Roussin; no flip) — iShares Core High Dividend ETF is the second of the video's '2 MUST OWN ETFs' and remains an important holding: higher-yield, more defensive complement to SCHD and to growth/tech. Up 24% YTD stated (vs SPY +11%). No share price stated.
calls.base_case: Tracks the Morningstar Dividend Yield Focus Index; emphasis on high-yield payers meeting financial criteria; 3%+ yield, 0.08% expense ratio, ~80 holdings, top sectors staples, energy, healthcare and utilities — the four best performers the past month — with tech only ~1%.
calls.bull_case: Its defensive sector mix has benefited while tech has sold off (QQQ down >6% in two weeks stated, S&P 500 down ~2%), giving a growth portfolio a different return driver.
calls.bear_case: Concentrated: top 10 are 55% (XOM, CVX, ABBV, VZ, PG, PM, HD, KO, PEP, MO stated) and energy concentration means a sharp oil fall could hit it even if other defensive holdings stay stable; it lacks SCHD's dividend-growth record and is not a substitute for a fully diversified portfolio.
